reasons: The lake record is verified and identifies the case as NASA v. FLRA in the U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1999-06-17, docket 98-369.
The lake citations list 527 U.S. 229, 119 S. Ct. 1979, 144 L. Ed. 2d 258, and 1999 U.S. LEXIS 4190, matching the payload.
The lake scope note says this is a statutory FSLMRS representation-rights holding, distinct from the Fifth Amendment Garrity line but grouped for the public-employee compelled-interview context.

The opinion concerns federal employee union representation during an OIG investigatory interview that could lead to discipline, so the 'Related (cross-doctrine)' home role is supported rather than overstating it as a Garrity holding.

The opinion frames the question as whether a NASA-OIG investigator can be considered a representative of NASA when examining a NASA employee so that the FSLMRS union-representation right may be invoked, and says the answer is affirmative.

The opinion states it was undisputed that the employee reasonably believed discipline could result, requested union representation, NASA was the relevant agency, and a violation occurred if section 7114(a)(2)(B) applied.
The Court concluded that the investigator was acting as a representative of NASA for purposes of section 7114(a)(2)(B) and affirmed.
residual_risks: The holding summary is supportable, but it is compressed; readers should not miss the statutory prerequisites that the employee be in the unit and request representation.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: For maximum precision, say the right applies to a bargaining-unit employee who requests representation and reasonably believes the examination may result in discipline.
